title: Recommendation Factory
blurb: Run a streaming service. Learn a viewer's taste and recommend what they'll actually love.
objectives: How it learns your patterns from feedback
Why random recommendations drive people away

glossary.def: An AI that suggests things you might like, based on what you've liked before.
What someone tends to enjoy — their taste.
How often your recommendations actually land (they watch / enjoy it).
Signals like thumbs up/down or watch time that teach the system your taste.

steps.title: Your streaming service
steps.body:
You just launched a streaming app. Thousands of titles, and every viewer wants the app to *just know* what to play next.

That's a **recommendation system** — and you're about to be one. Your job: figure out a viewer's taste and suggest things they'll love.

steps.title: What keeps viewers around?
steps.prompt: Which app keeps people watching longer?
choices: One that learns your taste and matches it
steps.afterPick: Matching taste wins — that's why your feed feels personal. Let's see it in action. →

steps.title: Recommend to this viewer
steps.youWillDo: recommend titles that match the viewer's taste
steps.body: Check the viewer's **likes and dislikes** at the top. For each title, **Recommend** it or **Skip** it. Matches get watched (a hit!); mismatches make them bounce. Try to keep your **hit rate** high — then hit **Recommend at random** to see what a clueless feed does.

steps.title: You learned their patterns
steps.body:
Good recommendations weren't luck — you used the viewer's **patterns** (loves space + action, hates romance) to predict what they'd enjoy.

When you recommended at random, the hit rate cratered and they bounced. Real apps learn from your **feedback** — thumbs, watch time, skips — to keep improving.

steps.title: How does it work?
steps.question: How does a recommendation system decide what to suggest?
choices: It finds patterns in what you've liked and predicts more like it
It shows everyone the exact same thing
It asks you to type what you want every time
steps.explain: Patterns in your past behavior → predictions about what you'll enjoy next. The more feedback, the sharper it gets.

steps.title: Say it your way
steps.prompt: How does an app like a music or video service seem to 'know' what you like?

recall.question: A recommender gets better mainly by…
choices: Learning from your feedback and patterns
recall.explain: Your likes, skips, and watch time teach it your taste.

steps.title: It's everywhere 🎉
steps.body:
You just built the idea behind the feeds you use every day — video apps, music, shopping, and social media all run **recommendation systems**.

They learn your patterns to predict what you'll enjoy. **Next up:** discover what all this AI actually *costs* to run.
